title: Translators' renderings of manna's appearance
english: Now the manna was as coriander seed (Numbers 11:7). The rest render it as bdellium; another says “from honey”; Aquila and Symmachus say “oil of the breast, oil into the lip.”
orientation: Origen is beginning his notes on Numbers by comparing how the Septuagint and other Greek translators render the description of manna in Numbers 11:7.

title: Miriam's leprosy as a warning to the people
english: When Miriam reviled Moses, she was struck with leprosy and sat outside the camp for seven days (Numbers 12:15). This happened for the fear of the people. For if he did not spare his sister, neither will he spare another.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Numbers 12, where Miriam spoke against Moses and was struck with leprosy.

title: The spies made God a liar by slandering the land
english: Verse 36. And the men. Those who slandered the land, piously in their own view, showed God—who praised the promised land—to be a liar.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Numbers 13:32, where the spies who scouted the promised land brought back a bad report, and he draws the moral conclusion that they made God a liar.

title: Balak's seeing and the nations' fear
english: Verse 2. And Balak having seen. Nations heard and were angered. Among them also were the Moabite rulers, and trembling seized them.
Verse 4. (23) Because they were bringing his fee as for a seer, to bring him forward.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Numbers 22:2, where Balak sees what Israel has done, and he connects this with a scriptural passage about nations hearing and being angry, with Moabite rulers seized by trembling.

title: Scripture prefers symbolic meaning over historical narrative
english: Verse 7. And having taken up his oracle. In certain places the divine Scripture prefers the symbolic meaning and sets it before the historical narrative in its own subject matter.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Numbers 24:7, where Balaam takes up his oracle, and he pauses to state a principle about how Scripture sometimes works.

title: Balaam's prophecy of a ruler and the Magi's tradition
english: Verse 7. And he will rule over many nations (Numbers 24:7). There are indeed many lords and many gods, but blessed are those who have our Lord Jesus Christ as Lord, for they will rule over many dominions.

Verse 17. And a man from Israel shall rise (Numbers 24:17). They say that Balaam had disciples in his art, men who had been instructed by him in magic, and that they held an opinion about him and wrote down his prophecies and left them behind, including the one that says, "A star shall rise." It was through receiving this from ancestral tradition and succession that the Magi came to Bethlehem.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Balaam's prophecy in Numbers, first on the ruler over many nations, then on the star prophecy and the tradition that the Magi inherited Balaam's prophecies.
